Diagnosis:
The test testNestedWithCommentsJDOM is failing due to trimming of string values automatically by JXPath. The test compares the retrieved string value from an XML element with expected values that contain leading or trailing spaces. The current bug report explicitly states that JXPath trims string values when it should preserve them.

Looking at the doTest method snippet and the test, the test calls doTest with the model set to DocumentContainer.MODEL_JDOM. This causes JXPath to use the JDOM model for XML processing.

Inspecting the getValue method of the JDOMNodePointer class (used when using the JDOM model), we see multiple conditions that handle different node types (Element, Comment, Text, CDATA, ProcessingInstruction).

- For Element nodes, it calls getTextTrim(), which trims spaces from the text content.
- For Comment nodes, it retrieves the text and explicitly calls trim() on it.
- For Text and CDATA nodes, it again calls getTextTrim(), which trims spaces.
- For ProcessingInstruction, it trims the data text as well.

Thus, in all these relevant code paths, the text content of the nodes is being trimmed before being returned by getValue.

This explains the bug: leading and trailing spaces from elements and text nodes are trimmed inadvertently because the implementation always uses trimmed text getters for the JDOM model's getValue method. The test expects the spaces to be preserved exactly, but the code currently removes them.

Therefore, the root cause is the implementation of the getValue method in the JDOMNodePointer class that returns trimmed strings instead of the exact node content text, causing JXPath to always trim string values automatically in the JDOM XML model.

Because recent bug reports are empty, no other clues influence this conclusion. The main fix is to modify JDOMNodePointer.getValue to avoid trimming text if it is not intended.

Suggested fix location: JDOMNodePointer.getValue()
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test `testNestedWithCommentsJDOM` uses the JDOM model within JXPath to retrieve XML string values. The current bug report indicates that JXPath trims strings when they contain leading or trailing spaces, which is unwanted. Upon inspecting the `JDOMNodePointer.getValue()` method, which is the value retrieval method for this model, we see that for relevant node types (Element, Text, CDATA) it calls `getTextTrim()`, which explicitly trims all leading and trailing whitespace. Similarly, for Comment and ProcessingInstruction nodes, the code explicitly calls `trim()` on the retrieved text. This consistent trimming within `getValue()` causes JXPath to never return the original string value verbatim, stripping any leading or trailing spaces. This matches the reported problem where values such as `<value> 12324 56</value>` are returned trimmed. The root cause is the implementation choice in the JDOM model pointer's `getValue()` method that enforces trimming rather than returning raw text content. The failure is thus explained by this trimming behavior in `JDOMNodePointer.getValue()`.

Recommended location to fix this issue is `JDOMNodePointer.getValue()` to avoid automatic trimming of string content values.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
